dervis-irab:1-4.t:
* Vocabulary:
(يَحْتَسِبُوا): [that] it should occur to their minds and they should think.
(الْجَلاءَ): leaving the homeland. Al-Rāzī said: «الجلاء is more specific than الخروج, because it is only said of a group, whereas الإخراج is for a group and for one person.» In al-Mukhtār: «الجلاء, with fatḥa and lengthening: the clear matter; from it you say جلا الخبر يجلو جلاء, it became clear. الجلاء is also leaving the land, and also expelling; جلوا عن أوطانهم (they left their homelands) and جلاهم غيرهم (others expelled them); it is transitive and intransitive.» The wording of al-Miṣbāḥ:
«The active participle from the triliteral is جالٍ, like قاضٍ, and the group is جالية; and from this the people of the dhimma whom ʿUmar, may Allah be pleased with him, expelled from the Arabian Peninsula were called جالية. Then الجالية was transferred to the jizya taken from them, then it was used for every jizya taken, even if the one paying it had not left his homeland; so it is said "so-and-so was appointed over the جالية", the plural being الجوالي.» And in al-Asās: «جلوا عن بلادهم جلاء: exile befell them; أجليناهم عنها and جلوناهم (we exiled them). And it is said of people, when they had been turned towards something, surrounding it, then dispersed from it: they have been driven out from it and أجلوا عنه (they withdrew from it).»

* I'rab:
(سَبَّحَ لِلَّهِ ما فِي السَّماواتِ وَما فِي الْأَرْضِ وَهُوَ الْعَزِيزُ الْحَكِيمُ): سبّح is a past verb; لله is a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) سبّح — and it has been said that the lām is redundant (zāʾida); ما is the fāʿil (agent); في السموات is attached to an omitted [verb], which is the ṣila (relative clause) of the relative noun; ما في الأرض is conjoined to ما في السموات; هو is a mubtadaʾ (subject), العزيز a first khabar (predicate) and الحكيم a second khabar.
(هُوَ الَّذِي أَخْرَجَ الَّذِينَ كَفَرُوا مِنْ أَهْلِ الْكِتابِ مِنْ دِيارِهِمْ لِأَوَّلِ الْحَشْرِ): the clause is resumptive or circumstantial. هو is a mubtadaʾ and الذي its khabar; the clause أخرج is the ṣila; الذين is the mafʿūl bihi (direct object); the clause كفروا is the ṣila of الذين; من أهل الكتاب is a ḥāl (circumstantial) from الذين كفروا — they are the Banū al-Naḍīr; من ديارهم is attached to أخرج; and لأول الحشر: this lām is attached to أخرج, and it is the lām of timing, as in His saying لدلوك الشمس, i.e. at the first gathering. The wording of al-Zamakhsharī: «لأول الحشر is attached to أخرج, and it is the lām in His saying يا ليتني قدّمت لحياتي, and in your saying "I came to him لوقت كذا (at such-and-such a time)".»
(ما ظَنَنْتُمْ أَنْ يَخْرُجُوا): ما is negating; ظننتم is a verb and its fāʿil; أن is a maṣdar-forming and accusative particle; يخرجوا is an imperfect verb, accusative (manṣūb) by أن; and أن with what lies in its scope fills the place of the two objects of ظننتم.
(وَظَنُّوا أَنَّهُمْ مانِعَتُهُمْ حُصُونُهُمْ مِنَ اللَّهِ): the wāw is conjunctive; ظنوا is a past verb, one of the verbs of the heart, and the wāw is the fāʿil; أنّ and its noun, which fills the place of the two objects of ظنوا; مانعتهم is the khabar of أنهم and حصونهم is the fāʿil of مانعتهم. It is also permissible that مانعتهم be a fronted khabar and حصونهم a postponed mubtadaʾ, the clause being the khabar of أنهم. من الله is attached to مانعتهم.
(فَأَتاهُمُ اللَّهُ مِنْ حَيْثُ لَمْ يَحْتَسِبُوا وَقَذَفَ فِي قُلُوبِهِمُ الرُّعْبَ): the fāʿ is for conjunction with immediate sequence; أتاهم الله is a past verb, a fronted mafʿūl bihi and a postponed fāʿil, i.e. His command or His punishment came to them. من is a preposition; حيث is an adverb of place, indeclinable (mabnī) on the ḍamma, in the position of the genitive by من, and the preposition and its noun are attached to أتاهم; لم is a particle of negation, conversion and jussive; يحتسبوا is an imperfect verb, jussive (majzūm), the sign of its jussive being the dropping of the nūn, and the clause is in the position of the genitive by the adverb being annexed to it. قذف is conjoined to فأتاهم; في قلوبهم is attached to قذف; and الرعب is the mafʿūl bihi. الرعب is read with ḍamma on the ʿayn and with sukūn.
(يُخْرِبُونَ بُيُوتَهُمْ بِأَيْدِيهِمْ وَأَيْدِي الْمُؤْمِنِينَ): this clause may be resumptive, as if it were an explanation of the terror, or circumstantial from the pronoun in قلوبهم. يخربون is an imperfect verb and its fāʿil; بيوتهم is the mafʿūl bihi; بأيديهم is attached to يخربون; أيدي is conjoined to بأيديهم; and المؤمنين is the muḍāf ilayhi of أيدي. It has been read يُخْرِبون without doubling, from أخرب, and with doubling (يُخَرِّبون), from خرّب.
(فَاعْتَبِرُوا يا أُولِي الْأَبْصارِ): the fāʿ is the fāʾ al-faṣīḥa (the fāʾ of eloquence implying an omitted condition), i.e. if you have pondered this and understood it, then take admonition from their state and do not betray. اعتبروا is an imperative verb and its fāʿil; يا is a vocative particle; أولي is the one addressed (munādā), a muḍāf, accusative by the yāʾ because it is attached [in its inflection] to the sound masculine plural; and الأبصار is the muḍāf ilayhi.
(وَلَوْلا أَنْ كَتَبَ اللَّهُ عَلَيْهِمُ الْجَلاءَ لَعَذَّبَهُمْ فِي الدُّنْيا): the wāw is resumptive; لولا is a particle of non-occurrence due to existence; أن is maṣdar-forming, and it with what follows is interpreted as a maṣdar (interpreted maṣdar) in the position of the nominative as a mubtadaʾ whose khabar is omitted, its implied form being "موجود" (existent). كتب الله is a verb and its fāʿil; عليهم is attached to كتب; الجلاء is the mafʿūl bihi; the lām occurs in the answer of لولا; عذبهم is a past verb, a latent fāʿil and a mafʿūl bihi; and في الدنيا is attached to يعذبهم [Translator's note: so in the source; the verb in the verse is عذّبهم].
(وَلَهُمْ فِي الْآخِرَةِ عَذابُ النَّارِ): the wāw is resumptive; لهم is a fronted khabar; في الآخرة is a ḥāl; and عذاب النار is a postponed mubtadaʾ; meaning: if they escaped the punishment of this world, the punishment of the Hereafter lies in wait for them. The wāw may not be conjunctive, because that would lead to conjoining the clause to عذبهم في الدنيا, and that would require that they also escape the punishment of the Hereafter, since لولا requires the negation of the consequence with the occurrence of the condition.
(ذلِكَ بِأَنَّهُمْ شَاقُّوا اللَّهَ وَرَسُولَهُ): ذلك is a mubtadaʾ, the reference being to what was mentioned of the punishment of this world and the punishment of the Hereafter; بأنهم is the khabar of ذلك; أنّ and its noun, and the clause شاقوا is its khabar, the wāw being the fāʿil; الله is the mafʿūl bihi and رسوله is conjoined to الله.
(وَمَنْ يُشَاقِّ اللَّهَ فَإِنَّ اللَّهَ شَدِيدُ الْعِقابِ): the wāw is conjunctive; من is a jussive conditional noun in the position of the nominative as a mubtadaʾ; يشاق is the protasis (fiʿl al-sharṭ); الله is the mafʿūl bihi; and the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ) is omitted, its implied form being "يعاقب" (He will punish). The fāʿ is causal, and إنّ with its noun and its predicate. You may also make the fāʿ a linking fāʿ, the clause being in the position of the jussive as the apodosis; and the protasis and its apodosis are the khabar of the mubtadaʾ.

* Benefits:
History relates that the Banū al-Naḍīr, a band of the Jews, settled in Medina in expectation of Muhammad ﷺ. Then they betrayed the Prophet after having made a covenant with him, and sided with the idolaters against him. So the Messenger of Allah besieged them until they agreed to exile. They were the first of the people of the dhimma to be exiled from the Arabian Peninsula, and the last of them were exiled in the time of ʿUmar ibn al-Khaṭṭāb. So their exile was the first gathering (ḥashr) from Medina, and the last gathering was ʿUmar's exiling of them. It has also been said that the first gathering was their expulsion from their fortresses to Khaybar, and the last gathering their expulsion from Khaybar to Syria. Ibn al-ʿArabī said:
«The gathering is first, middle and last: the first is the exile of the Banū al-Naḍīr, the middle is the exile of the people of Khaybar, and the last is the Day of Resurrection.»

dervis-irab:5-7.t:
* Vocabulary:
(لِينَةٍ): اللينة, with kasra, is linguistically the maṣdar of لان (to be soft); what is meant here is the palm-tree of the "colours" (al-alwān), which are the varieties of palm other than the ʿajwa and the barniyya, these two being the best of palms. Its yāʾ comes from a wāw, changed because of the kasra before it, as in الديمة. It has also been said that اللينة is the noble palm-tree, as if they derived it from اللين (softness). Dhū al-Rumma said:
كأن قتودي مؤتها عش طائر ... على لينة سوقاء تهفو جنوبها
(As if my saddle-frames upon her were a bird's nest on a tall-trunked palm, swayed by the south wind.)
He is describing his she-camel. القتود are the wooden pieces of the saddle, made from القتاد, a hard thorny tree; اللينة is the palm-tree; السوقاء is long-trunked; الجنوب is a kind of wind, and the pronoun refers to the palm. He likened the saddle-frames on top of the camel to a bird's nest on top of the palm-tree. اللينة has the plural لين.
(أَفاءَ): He made it fayʾ, i.e. booty.
(أَوْجَفْتُمْ): you hastened. In al-Miṣbāḥ: «وجف الفرس والبعير وجيفا: it ran; and أوجفته, with the alif: I made it run; it is a quick pace in travel.»
(رِكابٍ): الركاب are camels, the singular being راحلة, with the plurals ركب, ركائب and ركابات. ركاب السحاب are the winds. الركاب is also what is hung on the saddle, in which the rider puts his foot [the stirrup]. Al-Farrāʾ said: «The Arabs apply the word الراكب only to the rider of a camel, and they call the rider of a horse فارس.»
(دُولَةً): with ḍamma on the dāl, and it has also been read with fatḥa — two dialectal forms: what turns (yadūlu) for a person, i.e. revolves, of fortune. One says دالت له الدولة (fortune turned in his favour) and أديل لفلان (victory was given to so-and-so).

* I'rab:
(ما قَطَعْتُمْ مِنْ لِينَةٍ أَوْ تَرَكْتُمُوها قائِمَةً عَلى أُصُولِها فَبِإِذْنِ اللَّهِ): ما is a jussive conditional noun in the position of the accusative as a fronted mafʿūl bihi (direct object) of قطعتم; قطعتم is a verb and its fāʿil (agent), in the position of the jussive as the protasis (fiʿl al-sharṭ); من لينة is a ḥāl (circumstantial); أو is a conjunction [the source has "واو"; Translator's note: evidently a misprint for "أو"]; تركتموها is conjoined to قطعتم; قائمة is the second object of ترك; على أصولها is attached to (mutaʿalliq) قائمة; the fāʿ links the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ); بإذن is a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to an omitted khabar (predicate) of an omitted mubtadaʾ (subject), i.e. "then cutting it was by the permission of Allah"; and the nominal clause is in the position of the jussive as the apodosis.
(وَلِيُخْزِيَ الْفاسِقِينَ): the wāw is conjunctive and what it is conjoined to is omitted, its implied form being "He permitted cutting them in order to gladden the believers and strengthen them, and to disgrace the hypocrites and the transgressors and humble them". The lām is the lām of causation; يخزي is an imperfect verb, accusative (manṣūb) by an implied أن after the lām, and the preposition and its noun are attached to the implied omitted [verb]; and الفاسقين is the object of يخزي.
(وَما أَفاءَ اللَّهُ عَلى رَسُولِهِ مِنْهُمْ فَما أَوْجَفْتُمْ عَلَيْهِ مِنْ خَيْلٍ وَلا رِكابٍ): a resumptive statement brought to begin explaining the status of what was taken from their property. ما is a relative noun in the position of the nominative as a mubtadaʾ; the clause أفاء is the ṣila (relative clause) and الله is the fāʿil; على رسوله is attached to أفاء; منهم is a ḥāl; the fāʿ is linking, because of the flavour of condition in the relative; ما is negating; أوجفتم is a verb and its fāʿil; عليه is attached to أوجفتم; من is a redundant (zāʾida) preposition; خيل is genitive by من in form and accusative in position as the object of أوجفتم; and ولا ركاب is conjoined to خيل.
(وَلكِنَّ اللَّهَ يُسَلِّطُ رُسُلَهُ عَلى مَنْ يَشاءُ): the wāw is circumstantial; لكنّ is a particle of rectification (istidrāk) and accusative; الله is its noun and the clause يسلط its predicate; رسله is the mafʿūl bihi of يسلط; على من يشاء is attached to يسلط; and the clause يشاء is the ṣila of من.
(وَاللَّهُ عَلى كُلِّ شَيْءٍ قَدِيرٌ): الله is a mubtadaʾ; على كل شيء is attached to قدير; and قدير is the khabar of الله.
(ما أَفاءَ اللَّهُ عَلى رَسُولِهِ مِنْ أَهْلِ الْقُرى فَلِلَّهِ وَلِلرَّسُولِ وَلِذِي الْقُرْبى وَالْيَتامى وَالْمَساكِينِ وَابْنِ السَّبِيلِ): a resumptive statement brought to explain the uses to which the fayʾ is put; the secret of the faṣl (asyndeton) in it will come. ما is a relative noun, a mubtadaʾ; the clause أفاء is the ṣila and الله is the fāʿil; على رسوله is attached to أفاء; من أهل القرى is a ḥāl — Muqātil said: meaning Qurayẓa, al-Naḍīr and Khaybar. The fāʿ is linking because of the meaning of condition the relative contains; لله is the khabar of ما; and للرسول and what follows it are conjoined to لله.
(كَيْ لا يَكُونَ دُولَةً بَيْنَ الْأَغْنِياءِ مِنْكُمْ): كي is a particle of causation and genitive, in the sense of the lām; لا is negating; يكون is a defective imperfect verb, accusative by an implied أن after كي; the noun of يكون is latent, referring to the fayʾ; دولة is its predicate; بين الأغنياء is an adverb attached to an omitted adjective of دولة, i.e. that they circulate it among themselves; and معكم [Translator's note: so in the source; the verse has منكم] is a ḥāl.
(وَما آتاكُمُ الرَّسُولُ فَخُذُوهُ وَما نَهاكُمْ عَنْهُ فَانْتَهُوا): the wāw is conjunctive; ما is a relative noun in the position of the accusative as the mafʿūl bihi of an omitted verb indicated by خذوه — it is also permissible to parse the clause فخذوه as the khabar. The clause أتاكم is the ṣila; the kāf is the mafʿūl bihi and الرسول the fāʿil; the fāʿ is linking because of the flavour of condition in the relative; خذوه is an imperative verb, its fāʿil and its mafʿūl bihi; and وما نهاكم عنه فانتهوا is conjoined to what precedes.
(وَاتَّقُوا اللَّهَ إِنَّ اللَّهَ شَدِيدُ الْعِقابِ): اتقوا الله is an imperative verb, its fāʿil and its object; and إنّ with its noun and its predicate.

* Rhetoric:
In His saying «ما أفاء الله على رسوله» (the verse) there is faṣl (disjunction), which is leaving a clause unconjoined to another; its opposite is waṣl (conjunction), which is conjoining some clauses to others. This chapter is the most obscure of the chapters of ʿilm al-maʿānī, so much so that someone was asked: What is eloquence?
He said: Knowing faṣl and waṣl. [A versifier] said:
الفصل ترك عطف جملة أتت ... من بعد أخرى عكس وصل قد ثبت
(Faṣl is leaving unconjoined a clause that comes after another — the reverse of waṣl, as established.)
Each of them has places, which we summarise in what follows:
Places of faṣl: faṣl is obligatory in five places:
1- That there be complete unity between the two clauses, in that the second is a badal (substitute) of the first, as in the verse we are dealing with; or an explanation of it, as in «فوسوس إليه الشيطان قال يا آدم هل أدلك على شجرة الخلد»; or an emphasis of it, as in «فمهل الكافرين أمهلهم رويدا». In this place it is said that between the two clauses there is perfect connection (kamāl al-ittiṣāl).
2- That there be complete difference between the two clauses, in that they differ as statement (khabar) and performative (inshāʾ), as in [the poet's] saying:
لا تسأل المرء عن خلائقه ... في وجهه شاهد يغني عن الخبر
(Do not ask a man about his character; in his face is a witness that makes enquiry needless.)
And the saying of another:
وقال رائدهم أرسوا نزاولها ... فحتف كل امرئ يجري بمقدار
(Their scout said: Anchor here, we will engage it [the war]; for every man's death runs by a measure.)
So he did not conjoin نزاولها to أرسوا, because it is a statement in wording and meaning, while أرسوا is performative in wording and meaning. الرائد is the one who goes ahead of the people seeking water and pasture to camp at. His saying أرسوا means: stay at this pasture, suited for war; it is taken from أرسيت السفينة, i.e. I held the ship with the anchor. His saying نزاولها means: we will attempt the business of war and grapple with it. His saying فحتف etc. is the reason for something omitted that what precedes conveys, i.e. and let not fear of death (الحتف) prevent you from attempting to wage war by undertaking its tasks, for every [man's death]... etc. Now, there is disagreement about the i'rab of the clause نزاولها. It has been said that it has no grammatical position because it is a reason for what precedes it, and thus an answer to an implied question; so the faṣl is not due to perfect separation but to quasi-perfect connection. It has also been said that it is a ḥāl, i.e. stay in a state of engaging in war; hence the faṣl is not due to perfect separation, but because a ḥāl is not conjoined to the clause it qualifies. — Or [the second place is] that there be no relation in meaning between the two, as in your saying: "ʿAlī is a writer; the pigeon is a flyer." In this place it is said that between the two clauses there is perfect separation (kamāl al-inqiṭāʿ).
3- That the second clause be an answer to a question arising from the first clause, as in the saying of Allah the Exalted: «وما أبرىء نفسي إن النفس لأمّارة بالسوء». It is said that between the two clauses there is quasi-perfect connection (shibh kamāl al-ittiṣāl).
4- That a clause be preceded by two clauses, to one of which it may properly be conjoined because of the presence of a relation, while conjoining it to the other would corrupt [the meaning]; so conjunction is abandoned to prevent a false impression, as in [the poet's] saying:
وتظنّ سلمى أنني أبغي بها ... بدلا أراها في الضلال تهيم
(Salmā thinks I seek a substitute for her; I see her wandering in error.)
The clause أراها could properly be conjoined to تظن, but this is prevented by the false impression of its being conjoined to the clause أبغي بها, so that the third clause would be among the things Salmā supposes, although that is not intended. It is said that between the two clauses there is quasi-perfect separation (shibh kamāl al-inqiṭāʿ).
5- That it is not intended to make the two clauses share in the judgement, because of an impediment, as in the saying of Allah the Exalted: «وإذا خلوا إلى شياطينهم قالوا: إنا معكم إنما نحن مستهزئون الله يستهزىء بهم». The clause الله يستهزىء بهم cannot properly be conjoined to إنا معكم, since that would imply that it is part of what they said; nor to the clause قالوا, since that would imply that Allah's mocking them is restricted to the time of their being alone with their devils. It is said that in this place there is an intermediate state between the two perfections (tawassuṭ bayna al-kamālayn).
Places of waṣl: waṣl is obligatory in the following places:
1- When the two clauses agree as statement or performative, and there is a uniting aspect between them, i.e. a complete relation, and there is no impediment to conjunction, as in the saying of Allah the Exalted: «إن الأبرار لفي نعيم وإن الفجّار لفي جحيم», the uniting factor between them being contrast; and as in «كلوا واشربوا ولا تسرفوا», the uniting factor between them also being contrast, and it is an estimative (wahmī) one. That is because the estimative faculty treats contrast as the intellect treats correlation: just as the intellect is not presented with one of two correlatives without the other being presented to it, so the estimative faculty is not presented with one of two contraries without the other being presented to it.
2- When leaving out the conjunction would give an impression contrary to what is intended, as when you are asked: "Has ʿAlī recovered from the illness?" and you say "No", wishing to pray for the questioner; then waṣl is necessary, and you say "لا ورعاك الله" (No — and may Allah protect you), since if you used faṣl it might be imagined to be a prayer against the person addressed, that he not be protected. Were it not for this false impression, faṣl would be obligatory, since they differ as statement and performative.
3- That the first clause have a grammatical position, such as being a khabar, and it is intended that the second share with it in the ruling of that i'rab, as in: زيد قام أبوه وقعد أخوه (Zayd — his father stood and his brother sat).
Furthermore, the uniting factors are three: rational, estimative and imaginative. Its being rational means that it connects the two clauses and unites them before the thinking faculty by means of the intellect, as with likeness: for when the intellect turns to two things alike in reality and strips them of accidents, plurality disappears and they become one thing in that reality, so they come together in conjunction; but what is meant by likeness here is that they have a particular reality with an additional attribute. Its being estimative means that the estimative faculty contrives to unite them before the thinking faculty, as with closeness owing to the resemblance between white and yellow; the estimative faculty uses it to unite them, even though that resemblance is rational, because it takes it from the intellect and unites by it; and were it not for the estimative faculty the uniting would not be valid, because the intellect rejects the uniting, perceiving the difference along with it, while the estimative faculty makes it like likeness. Its being imaginative means that the imagination contrives the uniting before the thinking faculty, and this is the association of the two conjoined things in the thinking faculty; even if the association is rational, the estimative faculty takes it from it and unites by it. Since the imaginative uniting factor is this association, it differs as people differ: many a person has images associated in his mind that would never occur together in another's mind at all.

* Benefits:
History relates that when the Messenger of Allah ﷺ descended upon the Jews of the Banū al-Naḍīr, who had fortified themselves in their fortresses, he ordered their palm-trees to be cut down and burned. At that the enemies of Allah became distressed and said: "O Muhammad, you claimed that you desire righteousness; is it righteousness to cut down trees and palms? Have you found, in what you claim was sent down to you, corruption in the land?" The Muslims felt something in themselves at their words and feared that this might be corruption, and they disagreed about it: some of them said, "Do not cut them down, for it is part of what Allah has given us as fayʾ", and some said, "Rather, we will enrage them by cutting them down." So Allah sent down «ما قطعتم من لينة» (the verse).

dervis-irab:8-10.t:
* Vocabulary:
(خَصاصَةٌ): need and want; its origin is خصاص البيت, i.e. the gaps (openings) of the house.
(يُؤْثِرُونَ): الإيثار is giving preference to another over oneself. One says آثرته بكذا, i.e. I singled him out for it and preferred him.
(شُحَّ): الشحّ is greed for wealth. The difference between it and البخل (miserliness) is that الشحّ is an instinct, whereas البخل is the withholding itself; so it [الشحّ] is more general, because miserliness may exist without greed, but not the reverse. In al-Ṣiḥāḥ: «الشحّ is miserliness together with greed.»

* I'rab:
(لِلْفُقَراءِ الْمُهاجِرِينَ الَّذِينَ أُخْرِجُوا مِنْ دِيارِهِمْ وَأَمْوالِهِمْ): the parsers differed about what the preposition and its genitive noun are attached to (mutaʿalliq). Those inclining to the school of Abū Ḥanīfa made it a badal (substitute) of His saying لذي القربى and what is conjoined to it, which entails stipulating poverty in it; al-Zamakhsharī and Abū al-Baqāʾ followed this parsing. Those inclining to the school of al-Shāfiʿī attached it to an omitted [verb], its implied form being "أعجبوا" (wonder!), which entails not stipulating poverty, and that entitlement is by kinship; al-Suyūṭī and others followed this. The wording of Abū Ḥayyān: «Al-Zamakhsharī made it a badal of His saying ولذي القربى only because it is the school of Abū Ḥanīfa, the meaning being that the poor among the near kin are entitled; poverty is a condition according to the school of Abū Ḥanīfa, so al-Zamakhsharī interpreted it according to his school. As for al-Shāfiʿī, he holds that the cause of entitlement is kinship, so a rich kinsman takes [a share] because of his kinship.» [Translator's note: the source gives no closing quotation mark; the quotation is taken to end here.] The secret of the wonder is that the context indicates it, the meaning being: wonder at these emigrants, in that they left their homelands and their property and endured hardship of living and the bitterness of exile for love of the Prophet and of Islam. المهاجرين is a naʿt (adjective) of الفقراء and الذين a second adjective; the clause أخرجوا is the ṣila (relative clause); it is a past verb in the passive, and the wāw is the nāʾib fāʿil (deputy agent); من ديارهم is attached to أخرجوا; and أموالهم is conjoined to ديارهم. It was acceptable to express [their leaving] it as "going out from" it because wealth is like an enclosure that shelters its owner, so it was fitting to express it as going out.
(يَبْتَغُونَ فَضْلًا مِنَ اللَّهِ وَرِضْواناً): the clause is circumstantial, i.e. in the state of their seeking from Him the Exalted bounty and good pleasure. فضلا is the mafʿūl bihi (direct object); من الله is attached to يبتغون or to an omitted adjective of فضلا; and رضوانا is conjoined to فضلا.
(وَيَنْصُرُونَ اللَّهَ وَرَسُولَهُ أُولئِكَ هُمُ الصَّادِقُونَ): the clause is conjoined to the clause يبتغون; الله is the object of ينصرون and رسوله is conjoined to الله; أولئك is a mubtadaʾ (subject); هم is a pronoun of separation (ḍamīr faṣl) or a mubtadaʾ; and الصادقون is the khabar (predicate) of أولئك, or the khabar of هم, the clause then being the khabar of أولئك.
(وَالَّذِينَ تَبَوَّؤُا الدَّارَ وَالْإِيمانَ مِنْ قَبْلِهِمْ يُحِبُّونَ مَنْ هاجَرَ إِلَيْهِمْ): a resumptive statement brought to praise the Anṣār, who were kind to the emigrants and settled them in their abode. You may also make it coordinated with الفقراء. So on these two views الذين is either a mubtadaʾ, or conjoined to الفقراء and thus in the position of the genitive. The clause تبوءوا is the ṣila; الدار is the mafʿūl bihi; and الإيمان is the mafʿūl bihi of an omitted verb, its implied form being "وأخلصوا" (and made sincere), along the lines of [the poet's] saying: علفتها تبنا وماء باردا (I fed her straw and cool water). The conjunction is then a conjunction of clauses, because faith is not taken as a dwelling; so the speech was abbreviated. It has also been said that it involves the omission of a muḍāf, the meaning being "the abode of emigration and the abode of faith": the definite article in الدار was put in place of the muḍāf ilayhi, and the muḍāf was omitted from دار الإيمان and the muḍāf ilayhi put in its place. Or it is accusative by تبوءوا after it is made to carry the meaning of لزموا (they kept to), as if He said "they kept to the abode and kept to faith". It has also been said that it is a conjunction of single words, the figurative usage lying in الإيمان by way of metaphor. Further discussion of it will come in the section on rhetoric. من قبلهم is a ḥāl (circumstantial); the clause يحبّون is the khabar of الذين; من is the mafʿūl bihi; the clause هاجر is the ṣila; and إليهم is attached to هاجر.
(وَلا يَجِدُونَ فِي صُدُورِهِمْ حاجَةً مِمَّا أُوتُوا): the wāw is conjunctive; لا is negating; يجدون is an imperfect verb, nominative (marfūʿ), and the wāw is the fāʿil (agent); في صدورهم is attached to يجدون; حاجة is the mafʿūl bihi; مما is an adjective of حاجة; and the clause أوتوا is the ṣila of ما.
(وَيُؤْثِرُونَ عَلى أَنْفُسِهِمْ وَلَوْ كانَ بِهِمْ خَصاصَةٌ): conjoined to what precedes; على أنفسهم is attached to يؤثرون; the wāw is circumstantial; لو is conditional; كان is a defective past verb; بهم is the fronted predicate of كان and خصاصة its postponed noun. Ibn ʿUmar said: A sheep was given as a gift to a man among the Companions of the Prophet ﷺ, and he said, "My brother so-and-so is in greater need of it," and sent it to him; and it kept being sent on, one after another, until nine households had passed it around and it returned to the first; then [the verse] was revealed.
(وَمَنْ يُوقَ شُحَّ نَفْسِهِ فَأُولئِكَ هُمُ الْمُفْلِحُونَ): the wāw is resumptive; من is conditional, in the position of the nominative as a mubtadaʾ; يوق is the protasis (fiʿl al-sharṭ), jussive (majzūm), the sign of its jussive being the dropping of the weak letter; it is an imperfect verb in the passive, and the nāʾib fāʿil is latent (mustatir), its implied form being "هو"; شحّ is the second mafʿūl bihi; the fāʿ links the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ); أولئك is a mubtadaʾ; هم is a pronoun of separation or a second mubtadaʾ; المفلحون is the khabar of أولئك or the khabar of هم, the clause then being the khabar of أولئك; the clause فأولئك etc. is in the position of the jussive as the apodosis; and the protasis and its apodosis are the khabar of من.
(وَالَّذِينَ جاؤُ مِنْ بَعْدِهِمْ يَقُولُونَ: رَبَّنَا اغْفِرْ لَنا وَلِإِخْوانِنَا الَّذِينَ سَبَقُونا بِالْإِيمانِ): الذين is a mubtadaʾ; the clause جاءوا is the ṣila; من بعدهم is attached to جاءوا; the clause يقولون is the khabar of الذين; ربنا is the one addressed (munādā), a muḍāf; اغفر is a verb of supplication, and its fāʿil is latent, its implied form being "أنت", and the clause is the object of the saying (maqūl al-qawl); لإخواننا is conjoined to لنا; الذين is an adjective of إخواننا; the clause سبقونا is the ṣila of الذين; and بالإيمان is attached to سبقونا.
(وَلا تَجْعَلْ فِي قُلُوبِنا غِلًّا لِلَّذِينَ آمَنُوا): the wāw is conjunctive; لا is prohibitive; تجعل is an imperfect verb, jussive by لا; في قلوبنا is in the place of the second object of تجعل and غلّا is its first object; and للذين is an adjective of غلّا, i.e. rancour.
(رَبَّنا إِنَّكَ رَؤُفٌ رَحِيمٌ): ربنا is the one addressed, a muḍāf; إنّ and its noun; رءوف is the first predicate of إنّ and رحيم its second predicate.

* Rhetoric:
In His saying «والذين تبوءوا الدار والإيمان» there is the device of concision (ījāz), whose discussion has preceded in detail. Here it is a kind in which some words are abbreviated and the whole comes in literal wording, but its abbreviation is of the abbreviation of figurative words; some call it "abbreviation by following" (ikhtiṣār al-ittibāʿ). For the implied form, as we set out in the section on i'rab, is: "they settled in the abode and made faith sincere", as Dhū al-Rumma said:
لما حططت الرحل عنها واردا ... علفتها تبنا وماء باردا
(When I took the saddle off her, arriving at the water, I fed her straw and cool water.)
i.e. "and gave her to drink"; and like the saying of ʿAbd Allāh ibn al-Zibaʿrā:
ورأيت زوجك في الوغى ... متقلدا سيفا ورمحا
(I saw your husband in battle, girded with a sword and a spear.)
i.e. "and carrying a spear".

* Benefits:
The i'rab of His saying «للفقراء» has a great effect on the direction of doctrine. The school of Abū Ḥanīfa, may Allah have mercy on him, is that the entitlement of the near kin to their share of the fayʾ is restricted to the poor, so that their rich do not become entitled to it. Al-Shāfiʿī, may Allah have mercy on him — according to what Imām al-Ḥaramayn transmitted from him — was severe in refuting this school, [arguing] that Allah the Exalted tied entitlement to kinship and did not stipulate need, and that disregarding kinship is contradiction and opposition [to the text]. Imām al-Ḥaramayn offered an excuse for Abū Ḥanīfa: since alms were forbidden to them, the benefit of mentioning them in the fifth of the fayʾ and booty is that it is not forbidden to spend that on them as the spending of alms [on them] is forbidden. He then followed this excuse by saying:
It is not proper to express it thus, for the form of the verse explicitly states their entitlement, as an honour to them and a notice of the greatness of their rank; so whoever takes it to mean the permissibility of spending on them, with this permissibility countered by the permissibility of depriving them, has nullified the import of the verse. Then the Imām considered it grave that this should befall them, because they hold that faith is a condition in the slave [freed in expiation] of ẓihār, in addition to the text, and they establish that by analogy, since it is deduced and it is not of the kind that is established by analogy. He said: likewise it is incumbent on them to hold that stipulating poverty in the kinship and stipulating need [is] for the closeness of what they mentioned with the purpose of closeness [Translator's note: this sentence is garbled in the source; translated as written]; but since their basis is those singled out by lineage from the Messenger, upon him be blessing and peace, and those sprung from his tree, like the ʿajma [Translator's note: so in the source; the sense is unclear], no ground remains for their school with this.
End of the Imām's words. I have cited it only so that it may be known that his opposition to Abū Ḥanīfa assumes that the stipulation of need, according to Abū Ḥanīfa, rests on analogy or similar causes external to the verse; that is why he held him bound to [admit] it is an addition to the text. But since Abū Ḥanīfa derived the consideration of need from the qualification of this badal mentioned in the verse, one must take another path with him, and say that it is a badal of المساكين only. Its explanation is that He, glory be to Him, wished to describe the needy (al-masākīn) with attributes that confirm their entitlement, and to praise the rich for their preferring [others] and for not finding in their breasts any need for what they were given. Since that was His aim, and He had separated between the mention of them and the intended mention of their attributes by His saying:
«كيلا يكون دولة بين الأغنياء منكم» up to His saying «شديد العقاب», He refreshed the mention of them (taṭriya) to prepare for the successive attributes after it. So He mentioned them with another attribute suited to the first attribute and substituted for it, namely poverty, so that the refreshing would testify to the benefit of combining for them the two attributes of neediness and poverty. Then their attributes were recited after that, namely their being expelled from their homes and property as emigrants, and their seeking bounty and good pleasure from Allah. For the near kin were mentioned with an unrestricted attribute, so the basis is that they remain so until it is established that they are intended by the restriction; and what we have mentioned, of applying that to the needy, suffices to keep the speech balanced, so the near kin remain on the basis of unrestrictedness. That is a rule the Ḥanafīs cannot contest, for they hold that an exception following several clauses is specific to the last clause, because its referring to that keeps the speech balanced and what precedes remains on the basis; and there is no difference between following [clauses] with an exception and with a badal, and everything else besides. Moreover, if it were made a badal of ذوي القربى together with what follows it, its substitution for ذوي القربى could only be a substitution of part for whole, for the near kin are divided into poor and rich; while its substitution for المساكين could only be a substitution of a thing for the thing [itself], both referring to one and the same entity. It would then follow that this badal is felt [Translator's note: "محسوسا" in the source; perhaps for "مخصوصا", "specified"] as both of the two kinds mentioned at one time, and that is impossible because of the difference and disparity between the two kinds, each of them requiring what the other rejects. This much, Allah the Exalted willing, suffices [Translator's note: the source reads "كان", evidently for "كاف"]. On this basis al-Zajjāj parsed the verse, making it a badal of المساكين specifically. And Allah the Exalted grants success to what is right.

dervis-irab:11-17.t:
* I'rab:
(أَلَمْ تَرَ إِلَى الَّذِينَ نافَقُوا يَقُولُونَ لِإِخْوانِهِمُ الَّذِينَ كَفَرُوا مِنْ أَهْلِ الْكِتابِ): a resumptive statement brought to relate what passed between the hypocrites and the disbelievers of false statements and incoherent exchanges. The hamza is for the interrogative of affirmation (istifhām taqrīrī); لم is a particle of negation, conversion and jussive; تر is an imperfect verb, jussive (majzūm) by لم, the sign of its jussive being the dropping of the weak letter, and the fāʿil (agent) is a latent (mustatir) pronoun, its implied form being "أنت", i.e. "[do you not] look"; إلى الذين is a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) تر; the clause نافقوا is the ṣila (relative clause); the clause يقولون is resumptive, explaining what is wondered at, and the imperfect is used to make the image of the saying present and to convey its recurrence; لإخوانهم is attached to يقولون; الذين is a naʿt (adjective) of إخوانهم; the clause كفروا is the ṣila of الذين; and من أهل الكتاب is a ḥāl (circumstantial).
(لَئِنْ أُخْرِجْتُمْ لَنَخْرُجَنَّ مَعَكُمْ وَلا نُطِيعُ فِيكُمْ أَحَداً أَبَداً): the clause is the object of their saying (maqūl al-qawl). The lām is the lām preparing for the oath (al-lām al-muwaṭṭiʾa lil-qasam); إن is conditional; أخرجتم is a past verb in the passive, in the position of the jussive as the protasis (fiʿl al-sharṭ), and the tāʾ is the nāʾib fāʿil (deputy agent); the lām is also [that of] the answer to the oath; نخرجن is an imperfect verb, indeclinable (mabnī) on the fatḥa because of its connection with the heavy nūn of emphasis, and the clause has no grammatical position because it is the answer to the oath; and the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ) of conditional إن is omitted. What is frequent in the speech of the Arabs is to retain the lām announcing the oath before the conditional particle. معكم is an adverb attached to نخرجنّ. The wāw is a conjunction; لا is negating; يطع [Translator's note: so in the source, for نطيع] is an imperfect verb, nominative (marfūʿ) because it is conjoined to the clause لئن أخرجتم; likewise His saying وإن قوتلتم. So the object of their saying is three clauses, and the verb came in the nominative, it and what follows, because they refer back to the ruling of the oath, not to the ruling of the condition, in accordance with the agreed rule that when the oath precedes the condition, the answer belongs to the oath. فيكم is attached to نطيع with a muḍāf omitted, i.e. "in forsaking you"; أحدا is the mafʿūl bihi (direct object); and أبدا is an adverb of the negation, also attached to نطيع.
(وَإِنْ قُوتِلْتُمْ لَنَنْصُرَنَّكُمْ): the wāw is conjunctive; إن is conditional, the lām preparing for the oath having been omitted before it; قوتلتم is a past verb in the passive, in the position of the jussive as the protasis; the lām is the answer to the oath; ننصرنّكم is an imperfect verb, indeclinable on the fatḥa because of its connection with the heavy nūn of emphasis; the apodosis of إن is omitted; and the clause has no grammatical position because it is the answer to the oath. The discussion of that has preceded.
(وَاللَّهُ يَشْهَدُ إِنَّهُمْ لَكاذِبُونَ): الله is a mubtadaʾ (subject) and the clause يشهد is the khabar (predicate); إنّ is a particle resembling the verb, its hamza being given kasra because of the occurrence of the shifted lām (al-lām al-muzaḥlaqa) in its predicate; the hāʾ is its noun and كاذبون its predicate.
(لَئِنْ أُخْرِجُوا لا يَخْرُجُونَ مَعَهُمْ): the lām prepares for the oath; إن is conditional; أخرجوا is an imperfect verb [Translator's note: so in the source; it is a past verb] in the passive, and the wāw is the nāʾib fāʿil; it is in the position of the jussive as the protasis; the apodosis of إن is omitted, indicated by the answer to the oath, which is the clause لا يخرجون; and معهم is an adverb attached to يخرجون.
(وَلَئِنْ قُوتِلُوا لا يَنْصُرُونَهُمْ): conjoined to what precedes, and like it in its i'rab.
(وَلَئِنْ نَصَرُوهُمْ لَيُوَلُّنَّ الْأَدْبارَ ثُمَّ لا يُنْصَرُونَ): also conjoined. His saying ليولّنّ:
the lām is the answer to the oath; يولّنّ is an imperfect verb, nominative, the sign of its nominative being the retention of the nūn, which was dropped because of the succession of similar letters; the wāw, dropped because of the meeting of two quiescent letters, is the fāʿil; الأدبار is the mafʿūl bihi; ثم is a conjunction; لا is negating; and ينصرون is an imperfect verb conjoined to يولّنّ, nominative like it. The pronouns refer to the Jews or to the hypocrites.
(لَأَنْتُمْ أَشَدُّ رَهْبَةً فِي صُدُورِهِمْ مِنَ اللَّهِ): the lām is the lām of inception (lām al-ibtidāʾ); أنتم is a mubtadaʾ and أشد the khabar; رهبة is a tamyīz (specification), and it is the maṣdar (verbal noun) of رهب in the passive here, because those addressed are feared, not fearing. So the question does not arise: how can the comparison of greater fear be sound, when they do not fear Allah — for if they feared Him they would abandon disbelief and hypocrisy? في صدورهم is an adjective of رهبة and من الله is attached to رهبة.
(ذلِكَ بِأَنَّهُمْ قَوْمٌ لا يَفْقَهُونَ): ذلك is a mubtadaʾ and بأنهم the khabar; أنّ and its noun, and قوم is its predicate; and the clause لا يفقهون is an adjective of قوم.
(لا يُقاتِلُونَكُمْ جَمِيعاً إِلَّا فِي قُرىً مُحَصَّنَةٍ أَوْ مِنْ وَراءِ جُدُرٍ): لا is negating; يقاتلونكم is an imperfect verb, nominative, with its fāʿil and mafʿūl bihi; جميعا is a ḥāl, i.e. all together; إلا is a particle of restriction; في قرى is attached to يقاتلونكم, and the pronoun refers to the Jews; محصنة is an adjective of قرى; أو is a conjunction; من وراء is conjoined to في قرى; and جدر is the muḍāf ilayhi; it is the plural of جدار, and it has been read in the singular.
(بَأْسُهُمْ بَيْنَهُمْ شَدِيدٌ تَحْسَبُهُمْ جَمِيعاً وَقُلُوبُهُمْ شَتَّى): the clause is resumptive, explaining their state, i.e. they are of the utmost strength and courage when fighting one another, but when they fight you they become weak and cowardly. بأسهم is a mubtadaʾ; بينهم is an adverb attached to شديد; شديد is the khabar; the clause تحسبهم is also resumptive; تحسبهم is an imperfect verb, and the fāʿil is latent, its implied form being "أنت"; the hāʾ is the first mafʿūl bihi and جميعا the second mafʿūl bihi; the wāw is circumstantial; قلوبهم is a mubtadaʾ and شتى its khabar, and the clause is circumstantial.
(ذلِكَ بِأَنَّهُمْ قَوْمٌ لا يَعْقِلُونَ): the i'rab of its counterpart has preceded shortly.
(كَمَثَلِ الَّذِينَ مِنْ قَبْلِهِمْ قَرِيباً ذاقُوا وَبالَ أَمْرِهِمْ): كمثل is the khabar of an omitted mubtadaʾ, its implied form being "مثلهم" (their likeness); الذين is the muḍāf ilayhi; من قبلهم is the ṣila of الذين; قريبا is an adverb attached to the omitted [notion of] being (istiqrār) to which من قبلهم is attached; you may also attach it to ذاقوا. Al-Zamakhsharī attached it to an implied muḍāf in the khabar, i.e. "like the existence of the likeness of the people of Badr, recently", i.e. the likeness of the Jews of Banū al-Naḍīr, in the exile, humiliation and abasement that befell them, is like the likeness of the people of Mecca in what also befell them on the day of Badr of defeat, captivity and killing; and his view is not far-fetched. ذاقوا is a verb and its fāʿil, and وبال أمرهم is the object.
(وَلَهُمْ عَذابٌ أَلِيمٌ): the wāw is resumptive; لهم is a fronted khabar; عذاب a postponed mubtadaʾ; and عظيم [Translator's note: so in the source; the verse has أليم] is an adjective, i.e. in the Hereafter.
(كَمَثَلِ الشَّيْطانِ إِذْ قالَ لِلْإِنْسانِ اكْفُرْ): كمثل is the khabar of an omitted mubtadaʾ, i.e. the likeness of the hypocrites in inciting the Jews to fight is like the likeness of Satan. إذا [Translator's note: so in the source, for إذ] is an adverb of past time attached to the [notion of] being to which the khabar is attached; you may also attach it to an omitted [word] as a ḥāl from مثل الشيطان, as if it were an explanation of it. The clause قال is in the position of the genitive by the adverb being annexed to it; للإنسان is attached to قال; and the clause اكفر is the object of the saying.
(فَلَمَّا كَفَرَ قالَ إِنِّي بَرِيءٌ مِنْكَ): the fāʿ conjoins to something omitted, i.e. "so he disbelieved; then when he disbelieved". لما is temporal (ḥīniyya), or a linking [particle] containing the meaning of condition; the clause كفر is in the position of the genitive by the adverb being annexed to it; the clause قال has no grammatical position because it is the apodosis of a non-jussive condition; إنّ and its noun, and بريء is its predicate; and منك is attached to بريء.
(إِنِّي أَخافُ اللَّهَ رَبَّ الْعالَمِينَ): the clause is a false justification of his disowning him, for otherwise he does not fear Allah. إنّ and its noun, and the clause أخاف الله is its predicate; and رب العالمين is a badal (substitute) of الله or an adjective of it.
(فَكانَ عاقِبَتَهُما أَنَّهُما فِي النَّارِ خالِدَيْنِ فِيها وَذلِكَ جَزاءُ الظَّالِمِينَ): the fāʿ is conjunctive; كان is a defective past verb and عاقبتهما is its fronted predicate, i.e. [the end] of the misleader and the misled; أنّ and what lies in its scope is the khabar [Translator's note: so in the source; on the parsing just given it is the noun of كان]; أنّ and its noun, and في النار is its predicate; خالدين is a ḥāl; فيها is attached to خالدين; the wāw is resumptive; ذلك is a mubtadaʾ, the reference being to the punishment; and جزاء الظالمين is the khabar of ذلك.

dervis-irab:18-24.t:
* I'rab:
(يا أَيُّهَا الَّذِينَ آمَنُوا اتَّقُوا اللَّهَ وَلْتَنْظُرْ نَفْسٌ ما قَدَّمَتْ لِغَدٍ): a resumptive statement brought to address the believers and give them admonition. اتقوا is an imperative verb, indeclinable (mabnī) on the dropping of the nūn, the wāw is the fāʿil (agent) and الله its object; the wāw is a conjunction; the lām is the lām of command; تنظر is an imperfect verb, jussive (majzūm) by the lām of command; نفس is the fāʿil; ما is the object of تنظر; the clause قدّمت is the ṣila (relative clause) of ما, the returning pronoun being omitted, i.e. قدّمته; and لغد is attached to (mutaʿalliq) قدّمت. "Tomorrow" was applied to the Day of Resurrection to represent it as near. Further discussion of the meaning of "tomorrow" will come in the section on rhetoric.
(وَاتَّقُوا اللَّهَ إِنَّ اللَّهَ خَبِيرٌ بِما تَعْمَلُونَ): He repeated the command to fear [Him] for emphasis. The clause إن الله خبير بما تعملون is the reason for the command to fear [Him]; and إنّ with its noun and its predicate.
(وَلا تَكُونُوا كَالَّذِينَ نَسُوا اللَّهَ فَأَنْساهُمْ أَنْفُسَهُمْ): the wāw is conjunctive; لا is prohibitive; تكونوا is a defective imperfect verb, jussive by لا; the wāw is its noun and كالذين its predicate; the clause نسوا الله is the ṣila of the relative noun. فأنساهم: the fāʿ is conjunctive; أنساهم is a verb, a latent (mustatir) fāʿil and a first mafʿūl bihi (direct object); and أنفسهم is the second mafʿūl bihi.
(أُولئِكَ هُمُ الْفاسِقُونَ): أولئك is a mubtadaʾ (subject); هم is a pronoun of separation (ḍamīr faṣl) or a second mubtadaʾ; and الفاسقون is the khabar (predicate) of أولئك, or the khabar of هم, the clause then being the khabar of أولئك.
(لا يَسْتَوِي أَصْحابُ النَّارِ وَأَصْحابُ الْجَنَّةِ): لا is negating; يستوي is an imperfect verb, nominative (marfūʿ); أصحاب النار is the fāʿil; and أصحاب الجنة is conjoined to أصحاب النار.
(أَصْحابُ الْجَنَّةِ هُمُ الْفائِزُونَ): a resumptive statement brought to explain the manner of the inequality. أصحاب الجنة is a mubtadaʾ; هم is a pronoun of separation or a second mubtadaʾ; and الفائزون is the khabar in either case. Its counterpart has preceded shortly.
(لَوْ أَنْزَلْنا هذَا الْقُرْآنَ عَلى جَبَلٍ لَرَأَيْتَهُ خاشِعاً مُتَصَدِّعاً مِنْ خَشْيَةِ اللَّهِ): a resumptive statement brought for comparison. لو is conditional; أنزلنا is a verb and its fāʿil; هذا is the mafʿūl bihi and القرآن a badal (substitute); على جبل is attached to أنزلنا; the lām links the answer of لو; رأيته is a verb, its fāʿil and its mafʿūl bihi; خاشعا is a second object or a ḥāl (circumstantial), since the seeing may be mental or visual; متصدعا is a second ḥāl or an adjective of خاشعا; and من خشية الله is attached to متصدعا.
(وَتِلْكَ الْأَمْثالُ نَضْرِبُها لِلنَّاسِ لَعَلَّهُمْ يَتَفَكَّرُونَ): the wāw is resumptive; تلك is a mubtadaʾ; الأمثال is a badal; the clause نضربها is the khabar; للناس is attached to نضربها; لعلّ and its noun, and the clause يتفكرون is its predicate.
(هُوَ اللَّهُ الَّذِي لا إِلهَ إِلَّا هُوَ): هو is a mubtadaʾ; الله is a first khabar; الذي is a naʿt (adjective); and the clause لا إله إلا هو is the ṣila. The i'rab of the word of testimony (kalimat al-shahāda) has preceded in detail in al-Baqara, so renew your acquaintance with it.
(عالِمُ الْغَيْبِ وَالشَّهادَةِ هُوَ الرَّحْمنُ الرَّحِيمُ الْمَلِكُ الْقُدُّوسُ السَّلامُ الْمُؤْمِنُ الْمُهَيْمِنُ الْعَزِيزُ الْجَبَّارُ الْمُتَكَبِّرُ): multiple predicates of Allah. The Most Beautiful Names of Allah have preceded.
(سُبْحانَ اللَّهِ عَمَّا يُشْرِكُونَ): سبحان is a mafʿūl muṭlaq (absolute object) of an omitted verb; عمّا is attached to سبحان; and the clause يشركون is the ṣila.
(هُوَ اللَّهُ الْخالِقُ الْبارِئُ الْمُصَوِّرُ): هو is a mubtadaʾ, and the Most Beautiful Names after it are predicates.
(لَهُ الْأَسْماءُ الْحُسْنى): له is a fronted khabar, الأسماء a postponed mubtadaʾ, and الحسنى an adjective. الحسنى is the feminine of الأحسن, which is an elative (ism tafḍīl), not the feminine of أحسن as counterpart to امرأة حسناء. In al-Qāmūs: «Do not say رجل أحسن as counterpart to امرأة حسناء; its reverse is غلام أمرد, but do not say جارية مرداء. One only says هو الأحسن intending the elative afʿal, its plural being أحاسن; and الحسنى, with ḍamma, is the opposite of السوءى.»
(يُسَبِّحُ لَهُ ما فِي السَّماواتِ وَالْأَرْضِ وَهُوَ الْعَزِيزُ الْحَكِيمُ): this has preceded at the beginning of the sura.

* Rhetoric:
In His saying «ولتنظر نفس ما قدّمت لغد» there is the indefiniteness of نفس and of غد. As for the indefiniteness of نفس, it expresses the fewness of the souls that look into what they have sent ahead for the Hereafter. As for the indefiniteness of غد, it is to magnify it and leave its matter vague, as if it were said: for a tomorrow whose true nature is not known because of its greatness.
